n: After failing to destroy the Nephites, the Lamanite armies return to the land of Nephi.
The Amalekites, bitter over their losses and unable to strike the Nephites, stir up the Lamanites against the Anti-Nephi-Lehies again.
Once more the converts refuse to fight and let themselves be killed — keeping their covenant.
Ammon and his brothers, deeply loved by these people who treated them like angels, are moved with compassion at the slaughter.

f.w: as though they were angels sent from God

n: They propose that the whole people flee to the Nephites in Zarahemla.

f.w: flee out of the hands of our enemies

n: The king fears the Nephites will kill them for all the murders and sins they had committed against them.

f.g: An understandable fear given their history.

n: Ammon offers to ask the Lord; if the Lord says go, will they go?
The king agrees — and offers to become the Nephites’ slaves to make up for their past crimes. Their humility runs deep.
Ammon says slavery is against Nephite law, established by his father Mosiah. They should instead rely on the Nephites’ mercy.

f.w: against the law of our brethren

n: The king insists: ask the Lord — if he says go, we go; otherwise we will stay and perish.

f.w: otherwise we will perish in the land
f.g: They will obey God, whatever the outcome.

n: Ammon inquires, and the Lord answers.
The Lord says: get these people out, for Satan grips the Amalekites, who stir others to kill them. This people is blessed, and I will preserve them.

f.w: Satan has great hold on the hearts

f.g: A promise kept for generations, as Alma 53 and 56 show.

n: Ammon tells the king all that the Lord said.

f.g: The king trusts revelation through Ammon.

n: The whole people gather their flocks and herds and go into the wilderness between the two nations, stopping near the Nephite border.
Ammon and his brothers will go ahead to Zarahemla to see whether the Nephites will receive them.
On the way, Ammon and his brothers meet Alma — the joyful reunion first mentioned in Alma 17.
Ammon’s joy is so great that it exhausts his strength and he falls to the ground — the third time he has been overcome this way.

f.w: swallowed up in the joy of his God

n: Mormon asks: isn’t this exceeding joy? Only the truly repentant and humble seeker of happiness receives such joy.

f.w: the truly penitent and humble seeker of happiness

n: Alma, Aaron, Omner, and Himni rejoice greatly too, though not to the point of collapse.

f.w: not that to exceed their strength
f.g: Their joy did not overpower them physically.

n: Alma brings them home to Zarahemla, and they report everything to the chief judge.
The chief judge asks the people to vote on admitting the Anti-Nephi-Lehies.
The people vote to give them the land of Jershon, on the east by the sea, south of Bountiful, as their inheritance.

f.g: The name may relate to a Hebrew word meaning “a place of inheritance.”

n: The Nephites will station armies between Jershon and Nephi to protect them, honoring their oath not to fight, which came from their deep repentance.
In return, the converts will help support the Nephite armies with part of their goods — protection in exchange for provision.
Ammon and Alma return to the camp with the news, and Alma tells the story of his own conversion along with Ammon’s.
Rejoicing, they settle Jershon and become known as the people of Ammon.
They join the Nephites and the church, known for zeal toward God and others, perfect honesty, and firmness in Christ to the end.

f.w: perfectly honest and upright in all things
firm in the faith of Christ

n: They regarded killing with horror and never feared death, because of their hope in Christ and the resurrection — death was swallowed up in Christ’s victory.
They would endure the cruelest death rather than take up sword or scimitar against their brothers.
They were a zealous, beloved, and highly favored people of the Lord.
